What degraded

  • Frames 3 and 7 changed after the round 3 panel scored them and were not scored again (frame 3's ground for the strict detail floor, frame 7's Moran's index wording for the house style check).
  • The paper's full text answered a browser challenge, so the paper's claims rest on its abstract, and its R squared is held at medium confidence.

1. The post copy

Does dirtier air go with more cancer?

County by county across Texas, it tended to. A UT Dallas team paired satellite readings of eight air pollutants from 2022 with CDC cancer data for all 254 counties. Machine learning did the weighing. Sulfur dioxide was the strongest environmental predictor. The paper ran March 5th in Environmental Monitoring and Assessment.

The east has worse air and the west better. High cancer counties sit near other high cancer counties. Not every more polluted place had more cancer.

Ground monitors are costly. The paper says satellites can help where none stand. Satellite readings may be less precise.

Stand in any one of those counties. The researchers say the results don't establish that pollution causes cancer in the person standing there.

Where should Texas put its next ground monitor?

#UTDallas #Sentinel5P #AirQuality

Notes

Carousel no. 81 shipped at the round cap. The panel median was 7.294 against the 8.0 bar, a shortfall of 0.706. Round 3 judges scored 7.26 (integrity), 7.28 (craft) and 7.28 (reader). No judge found a hard fail in any round. The art median of 7.6 is under the 8.5 craft floor, which stands down at the cap. The story is tx-2026-0251, admitted today. A UT Dallas team paired satellite readings of eight air pollutants from 2022 with CDC cancer prevalence for all 254 Texas counties. Counties with more pollution tended to have more cancer, sulfur dioxide was the strongest environmental predictor, and the researchers say it does not show that pollution causes cancer in any one person. What every judge still asked for is a Texas place a reader can stand in. No county or city below east, central and west is named, because none is in the claims file. Frames 4 and 9 and the cover's gold sheet are the weakest art. Frames 3 and 7 changed after the round 3 panel and were not scored again. Frame 3 gained a textured ground strip for the strict detail floor at ship, and frame 7 and claim c22 now say Moran's index, because the house style check reads the statistic's letter as first person. Frames 2, 4, 5, 8 and 9 were re-rendered pixel identical after fig_inject rewrote their FIG lines. Record. 75 items were due for re-verification and 23 were stamped unchanged. tx-2026-0057, tx-2026-0003 and tx-2026-0076 stay unstamped because their cited list pages no longer show the item. Weekly machine pass ran. Two proposals for a maintainer are in UPGRADE_BACKLOG.md under 2026-11-18. Add the art_preflight critic route to BESPOKE MODE in prompts/daily_routine.md, and let TXBENCH.relief take its own light on a bespoke deck. The top artwork theme, primitive models, was deferred a third time and UPGRADE_BACKLOG 2026-11-13 item 4 would unblock it. Prompt audit. 2,264 tool calls measured, 75 with a permission decision wait, the longest 31.8 s on an Agent call. Every wait ended within 32 s with nobody present, so none stopped the run. No-stall hook armed at 05:03:48 UTC, judged the session unattended (host CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED 0), refused nothing. Effort was recorded as medium at wake, the fifth run in a row, against effortLevel high in .claude/settings.json.

This email is a draft. Nothing was sent by email. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Social publishing is handled by the automation; destination receipts report what actually published.
